newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa money mkt shortage rises to 9.82 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: South Africa money mkt shortage rises to 9.82 bln rand.

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage rose to 9.823 billion on Thursday from 9.677 billion on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.

Dealers said the money market shortage remained extremely high for mid-month and pressure on liquidity was likely to continue until around the end of January with Christmas spending exacerbating the situation.
Three-month NCD rates were unchanged on Thursday morning at between 16.95 and 17.20 percent, having been increased on Wednesday. The 90-day BA rate was held at 16.30 to 16.75.

High money market rates this month have led to fears of an official interest rate hike. However, many economists believe the authorities will hold Bank rate at its current 16 percent pending data on October money supply and the third quarter current account due at the end of November and early December.
